### PDU41002 mains switching, over SERIAL — outlet 8, real contactor movement
### firmware 1.3.4 / captured 2026-08-24
### Nothing was plugged into the PDU. Outlet 8 was left On.
###
### THE CENTRAL FINDING: oltctrl returns NO confirmation of any kind. Compare
### the SWITCH-OFF response below with the PRE response — the command produces
### a blank line and a re-prompt, and nothing else. There is no "OK", no status,
### no error, and the response is byte-identical whether or not the outlet
### actually moved.
###
### That is why read-back verification is mandatory rather than prudent: the
### response cannot distinguish success from a no-op. verify=True re-reads
### oltsta index N show and compares.

### PRE — state before switching
### CMD: oltsta index 8 show
oltsta index 8 show

    Outlet8
    Outlet Name : Outlet8
    Status :      On

CyberPower >

### SWITCH-OFF — the write. Round trip 0.62s.
### CMD: oltctrl index 8 act off
oltctrl index 8 act off

CyberPower >

### POST-OFF — read back after ~2s settle. Status flipped to Off.
### CMD: oltsta index 8 show
oltsta index 8 show

    Outlet8
    Outlet Name : Outlet8
    Status :      Off

CyberPower >

### SWITCH-ON — the write. Round trip 0.63s.
### CMD: oltctrl index 8 act on
oltctrl index 8 act on

CyberPower >

### POST-ON — read back after ~4s settle. Restored to On.
### Note oltcfg reports a 3s on-delay and 3s off-delay per outlet, so the
### settle window must exceed the configured delay, not just the ~1.5s the
### contactor itself takes. A retry loop bounded at ~1.5s would flake here.
### CMD: oltsta index 8 show
oltsta index 8 show

    Outlet8
    Outlet Name : Outlet8
    Status :      On

CyberPower >

### FINAL — all 8 outlets confirmed On at end of capture.
### CMD: oltsta show
oltsta show

    #  Name                                 Status
    -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
    1  Outlet1                              On
    2  Outlet2                              On
    3  Outlet3                              On
    4  Outlet4                              On
    5  Outlet5                              On
    6  Outlet6                              On
    7  Outlet7                              On
    8  Outlet8                              On

CyberPower >

### Timing summary for the retry window
###   oltctrl command round trip:     ~0.62 s (both directions)
###   configured on/off delay:         3 s per outlet (oltcfg index all show)
###   configured reboot duration:      5 s per outlet
###   observed state settle:           within 2 s for off, within 4 s for on
### A read-back retry budget must therefore cover the CONFIGURED delay plus
### margin — the driver should derive it from oltcfg rather than hardcode it,
### because an operator can change td_on/td_off per outlet.
